name: Baby Poop Green
lede: Baby Poop Green is a dull yellow-green, a cooler variant of [[baby-poop|Baby Poop]] that the 2010 xkcd color survey's crowd of respondents named separately rather than folding into the same cluster.

sections.title: A modifier on an existing crowd name
sections.body:
The name comes from Randall Munroe's 2010 xkcd color survey, where visitors typed a word next to a swatch and the most common label for each cluster of clicks won [1]. Our data treats it as a family word under [[baby-poop|Baby Poop]], the "green" simply marking the cooler, more yellow-green member of that naming cluster [1]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file this patch as a deep greenish yellow, about 4.3 units off, with Munsell notation 2.1GY 5.9/9.0 [1].

The closest look-alike in our data is [[baby-shit-green|Baby Shit Green]], only 2.2 units away and from the same scatological cluster, with [[vomit-green|Vomit Green]] and [[pea-soup-green|Pea Soup Green]] also nearby [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, finds this yellow-green in 13 of them, about 0.05 percent, rarer than 65 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 4.8 times the expected rate for that century (7 of 1,674 paintings from then), and inside a painting it is most often an accent, 62 percent of the time, by lightness rank rather than raw area [2].

The earliest match in our archive is dated 1830, by Reuben Rowley, 180 years before the name itself appears in 2010 [2]. Our archive's early centuries are thin, so that date is a floor, not a first, and the match is only a look-alike hue, not proof the name or a matching dye existed then [2].
